observed.facings.png: Four facings at one scale. South: just two small dark iron hook ends. East: a short, thick timber ladder seen in a squeezed side view. Two heavy log stringers run roughly horizontally, with iron straps. Four or five vertical round rungs join them, and dark iron hooks sit on the right end. North: a face-on timber ladder. Two round wood stringers converge slightly downward, with about 8 round rungs whose gaps get smaller lower down. Outer guide rails carry iron straps and are topped by curled iron hooks. West: the east view mirrored.
observed.south.png: Two small dark iron hook curls near the lower middle of an otherwise empty canvas. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A side-view ladder in the lower right of the canvas. Thick log stringers at top and bottom, slightly skewed. Vertical round wood rungs between them. Iron bands and two black curled hooks on the right edge. Wood grain shading and a dark outline.
observed.north.png: A face-on wood ladder centred in the canvas. Round timber stringers and rungs with grain, plus outer guide rails with iron bands. Curled black iron hooks sit at the rail tops. The ladder narrows toward the bottom and the rung spacing tightens. No backdrop.
observed.west.png: Mirror of east, sitting in the lower left with the hooks on the left edge.
observed.scale.png: Composite pit scene with a vanilla human at the bottom left. The north ladder runs from the north rim hooks down the light wall band and stops at the dark pit floor. The east and west ladders sit on their light wall bands, hooks at the outer rim, ending at the edge of the dark floor. On the south rim only the two hooks show. The ladder is sized plausibly against the human.
observed.wall_context.png: Lowered and raised states side by side in the pit. Lowered: as in scale.png. Raised north: the ladder is slid up past the north rim onto the ground above, while its guide rails with hooks stay on the wall band below. Raised east/west: the ladder body is moved past the side rim toward the outside ground, with the rails still on the band. Raised south: a short ladder top shows above the near rim, between the hooks.
observed.variants_1.png: Raised north. The ladder (round stringers, about 7 rungs) stands higher, with its top well above the hooks. The outer guide rails with iron bands and hooks continue below the ladder's foot down to the band bottom. The ladder overlaps the rails where they meet.
observed.variants_2.png: Raised east. Guide rail stringers (thick logs with iron bands) sit at the left with hooks. The ladder section (vertical rungs between log stringers) is shifted right past them, overlapping at the bracket region.
observed.variants_4.png: Raised south. The top of a ladder (two posts, four rungs) stands up between two iron hook ends at the bottom.
observed.variants_5.png: Zoom sheet. North wall lowered: a ladder with converging rails, hooks over the black rim line, ending at the band bottom before the dark floor. North raised: the ladder slid up above the rim, rails continuing down the band. East lowered: the ladder spans the light band from the rim (hooks at the black line) leftward to the band edge, with heavy log stringers running east-west. East raised: the ladder shifted right past the rim, rails still on the band. West: mirror.

CAMERA.seen: The north view is face-on with depth convergence, consistent with the pit's wall-band convention. No round tops to judge.

BORE.seen: No pipes or hoses. The hooks are solid curls with no open bore shown.

PORTS.seen: The card lists no code ports and nothing is attached. wall_context stands in for the assembled view.

WALL_LEAN.seen: The east-wall ladder has its hooks at the east rim and runs leftward into the pit. The west ladder is mirrored at the west rim. Each matches its wall side, and the owner already approved the perspectives.

WALL_AXIS.seen: North: long axis screen-vertical, from the rim down the face. East/west: the stringers run screen east-west, from the rim hooks down onto the band toward the pit.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: No code ports and no drawn connectors; the hooks are rail tops, not ports.

LAYERS.seen: In the raised views the ladder draws over its rails at the bracket overlap, which is plausible since the ladder is in front of the rails.

ROTATIONS.seen: Same wood palette, iron hooks and straps, and round timber on every facing and state.

SIGNATURE.seen: A ladder on guide rails with rail tops curled over the rim. The raised state shows it slid up and still held by the rails.

MATERIAL.seen: Warm brown with visible grain, log ends and iron straps. It reads as timber.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Stays on the wall bands. The lowered E/W views end at the band edge without entering the dark floor. The raised extension past the rim is intended.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs on every facing, with no shadow or patch.

OURS.seen: Script-drawn art matching the mod's own v4 shape. Not vanilla or donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Open fire-escape spacing on the north view. The north wall look is kept. E/W are steep and stay on the band. Side stringers are now thick logs rather than skeletal lines. Rungs, stringers and rails are visibly heavier wood.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the north view still reads as a ladder with hooks. The side views read as a timber frame on the wall band.

reply.subject: RM_Ladder
reply.image_seen: Images 1–5 show four wooden ladder facings: south has two exposed hooks, north has converging rails and open rungs, and east/west have mirrored compressed frames. Image 6 shows scale beside a human; image 7 shows lowered and raised wall placements; image 8 shows raised north. The required assembled in-game capture is absent, preventing final acceptance.

concerns.evidence: In images 3 and 5, the thick stringers run across the narrow wall band and the rungs run vertically between them. Image 7 places these frames across the side-wall bands. This is the quarter-turned, squeezed ladder construction explicitly required by the card; its gate-like silhouette follows that convention.

In image 7's raised side views, the moving ladder projects outward past the rim while the hooked guide rails remain on the wall band. The ladder and rails overlap at both stringers, with dark retaining brackets visible in the overlap. The exposed rail tails match the raised north arrangement in image 8.
Images 2–5 and 8 show solid timber poles, rungs, iron straps and curled hooks. There is no pipe or hose opening to exhibit an incorrect bore plane; the bore check passes on the visible parts.
The card defines zero ports. The visible hardware consists of rim hooks and retaining brackets, with no drawn hose, cord or coupler connectors. The supplied part views show no missing or extra port.
